basis: s0003 「姚泓，字元子，興之長子也。」 names Yao Hong's father explicitly as 興. p002 Yao Xing owns that exact span (m0008, 興 at code points 7-8 of s0003), and p117's only personal-name claim (c0513, 姚興, explicit) cites the same s0003 and the same 興. Both records therefore rest on one and the same source token.

p117 is defined only as Yao Hong's father (c0514 'Father of Yao Hong' 姚泓之父; c1482 parent-of p089 Yao Hong; c1483 parent-of p086 Yao Yi, Hong's 母弟). A man has one biological father, and the chapter names that father as 興 in s0003, so p117 can only be Yao Xing; no unit gives Hong a different father.
p117 has no mention of its own; its mentionException records that its name is 'already spanned on p002'. It is a kinship-derived duplicate of p002, not an independent attestation of another person.

Chronology agrees: 「興既死，秘不發喪。」 (s0027) records Xing's death before Hong's accession, consistent with p117's undated attestation 'already dead before the accession'. Nothing in the chapter supports a second, different father-figure.
notes: The merge adds jinshu:119:p117 to Yao Xing's existing canonical per_04WA1VRNJPZ23CHB2NB1 (with p002); it creates no new canonical ID and touches no other pair.

s0130 「泓曰：「叔父之言，社稷之計也。」」 is weak evidence for p117. 叔父 there is Hong addressing his paternal uncle (Yao Shao), not his father, so it supports p117's paternal kinship only indirectly. The identity rests on s0003, not on s0130; I am not changing that claim's certainty.
Other Yao Xing records in this chapter (p193 子略 s0260, p201 興 s0276) are out of scope for this one-pair review and remain separate pending their own review.
No English repair: s0003 'Yao Xing’s eldest son' / 'the eldest son of Yao Xing' and s0027 'When Yao Xing died' / 'After Xing died' already render 興 correctly.
